blockNote: World map destination menus and their handlers (Bank 03, 242689-244449). WorldMapController runs world_map_options[choice id & $1F] with SwitchCase after SetSavedPtr(DeferSceneTransition); the chosen handler ends in RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to DeferSceneTransition.
=== A MENU (choice ids $01-$1B) ===

PrintDialogString shows a Quit / destination text, then COP DialogueOptions ( grid, skip, &list ) runs MenuSelectionHandler and jumps through the list; the RestoreSavedPtr that follows in the source is never reached (the RTI goes to the list target).

- grid byte: low nibble = items per column, high nibble = total items (0 when everything fits in one column): #01 Quit only, #02 two items, #32 three items, #42 four items. The text puts the second column after the spaces (Quit [N] ... = column one; the text after 8-12 spaces = column two).
- skip byte: text lines skipped before the first option row (#01 everywhere here). The cursor always starts on the first item, Quit.

- list index = MenuSelectionHandler result: 0 = B pressed, 1 = first item (column one, top), 2 = column one, second row, then column two top to bottom. So for #32 / #42 the list order is not the reading order of the text.
- Quit and B both run the same handler: QueueMapChange back to the scene the player came from, with no route (route id stays 0), so DeferSceneTransition dies and the scene changes at once.
=== HANDLERS ===

A trip handler is StageWorldMapMoveIds ( 0, route id ) followed by a QueueMapChange ( scene, X, Y, flags, scroll ) for the destination. Most handlers are two adjacent blocks: the first has no end and falls into the second (the second is also the Quit handler of the destination's own menu). Seven handlers hold both operations in one block. QueueMapChange flag bit 7 ($80) records the destination as the new revive / save point (Inca Ruins, Diamond Mine, Great Wall, Mt.Temple entrance, Angkor Wat, Pyramid). The Watermia to Euro handlers also write $0D60 := 7 (leader animation 7).

=== ROUTES (world_map_routes.asm, Bank 03 241015-242132; the merge tool cannot annotate that file: no bank information) ===

38 table entries ($00-$25) point at 37 route arrays; $00 aliases $01. A step is four bytes: three movement_delta_table indices (X $00CA, Y $00CC, rotation $00BC; 0 = still) and a tick count n. The extraction shows them as route-step < b0, b1, b2, b3 >, which the old header read as flags, direction, spare and distance; that reading is wrong. Every array is 4n + 1 bytes: a hidden $FF ends it; $FE (subroutine) is never used.

Indices used: X and Y take 1 (+1 per tick), 2 (-1), $11 (alternating +1, 0) or $12 (alternating -1, 0); rotation takes 1 (+1) or 2 (-1). Steps never mix rotation with movement: a route turns the map ($20 = 22.5 degrees, $40 = 45, $80 = 90, $C0 = 135) and runs straight in one of eight directions.

Check: summing the steps reproduces the distance between the staged start positions of the two scenes (overworld_exit): route $09 = 128 north, $03 = 16 west and 240 north, $0A = 224 east and 96 south ($0B the reverse), $01 = 48 east and 112 north. These match with n ticks per step; the engine code applies n + 1 deltas, which would add one pixel per axis step (OQ-I060-2).

blockNote: Palette animation bundles (bank $16 in the extraction, ROM bank $96; 128 bundles, ids $00-$7F). They are not compressed and nothing is decompressed: a bundle is a list of colour strips that the five palette COP handlers (#36-#3A, cop_handlers_palette) step through with LoadPaletteBundle / CopyPaletteBundleFrame (hdma_dma_spc).
=== FORMAT ===
- palette_bundles: 128 word pointers, indexed by the bundle id (animScratch+2 of the palette thinker or actor).

- A bundle is a list of 6-byte sub-entries, palette-bundle < N, &frames, dest, size, wait >, ended by a hidden 0 byte: N = number of frames in the strip (0 ends the bundle); &frames = address of the first frame; dest = first CGRAM colour index (the colours go to the staging buffer $7F0A00 + 2 x index); size = bytes per frame minus one ($0D = 7 colours, $0F = 8, $1D = 15, $1F = 16, $03 = 2, $02 = a backdrop RGB triplet); wait = extra ticks between frames.
- The word_16xxxx arrays are the frames, stored back to back (BGR555 words), N frames per strip.

Whole-file counts (not a sample): 132 palette_bundle_ blocks (128 in the table + 4 empty padding bundles, see below), 1,200 sub-entries, 834 frame arrays. The commonest (dest, size) pairs: ($21, $17) 446 times (12 colours at index $21), ($23, $19) 175, ($81, $1D) 143 (15 colours at $81-$8F: the player's sprite colours), ($80, $1F) 39, ($2A, $0B) 25, ($A1, $1D) 24, ($91, $1D) 24.

Known uses (not all traced): bundles #0B / #0C restore Will's / Freedan's colours ($81-$8F) after the attack tints (attack_ability_system); #2A / #2B / #4B / #2C / #5B are the attack and aura effects; #4A is the Dark Friar flash; ambient_palette_cycler lists the per-scene ambient strips ($30 for scenes 21-23 is a six-strip colour rotation); WorldMapController resets Will's colours with PaletteResetAndKillThinker #0B. What most bundles look like on screen was not traced.
